reason: Conversation 1 never answered the homeowner's repeated direct question about what to set the dial to, looping the same scripted prompts four times despite her already confirming the dial was on max and food was pressed against the vents; it gave no actionable guidance at all. Conversation 2 correctly identified the two most likely causes (max setting plus food blocking the rear vent), told her exactly what to do (mid setting, clear the back wall, wait 24 hours) and set a sensible threshold for escalation. Conversation 2's follow-up is its weakness: it declared one yoghurt freezing at the very back 'not normal' and jumped to a blocked defrost drain / defrost fault with a 24-hour manual defrost, rather than suggesting a thermometer check, keeping items off the back wall and monitoring before involving an engineer, which overstates certainty on a genuinely uncertain case. Both stayed within the safety boundary, so Conversation 2 wins clearly on usefulness and honest initial diagnosis, but not decisively given the overconfident final step.
